subject: Tier portability and fallback playbook
messages:
From: Alex Torres <atorres@wellpath.health>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: sally.greene@procurement.wellpath.health
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Tier portability and fallback playbook

Irene / Redwood team —

Thanks for the demo last week. We liked the Dedicated capacity option but procurement wants clarity on two things before we proceed:

1) If we later need to downshift from Dedicated -> Hosted, what features are preserved vs removed? (KV cache retention, per-route routing, observability retention)
2) How do proration and credits work for a mid-term downgrade or partial seat reduction? We have seasonal usage spikes and want a safe rollback path without disrupting routing rules.

I've attached our Q3 token/throughput export so you can run a mapping against our patterns. Would appreciate a short playbook (decision tree + pricing outcomes) we can show internal stakeholders.

Attachments: Wellpath_Q3_usage.csv (CSV export, 120KB)

Thanks,
Alex Torres
Director of AI Platforms
Wellpath Health
atorres@wellpath.health
(415) 555-0182

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Alex Torres <atorres@wellpath.health>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tier portability and fallback playbook

Alex — thanks for the file, that helps. High level answers up front:

- Feature preservation: routing policies and per-route model pinning persist in policy metadata for 30 days after a downgrade; KV cache (runtime-level) cannot be preserved when moving from Dedicated GPUs to Hosted shared runtimes — that will be a cold start for KV. Observability retention is configurable via the Console (we can extend logs/metrics retention for a fee if you need longer term).

- Proration & credits: we support pro-rata credits for unused committed Dedicated capacity on monthly contracts (we provide a formula in the amendment). Seat reductions that reduce committed throughput below a threshold require a 14-day notice to avoid a stepdown fee.

I want to propose two concrete outcomes for your team to review:

A) Downgrade-safe path (minimal runtime disruption): keep routing and model pin metadata -> move workloads to a Hosted-compatible variant (same model quantization). Accept cold KV restart; Redwood will pre-warm caches for top-3 routes during the transition window. Estimated one-time migration labor: 4 engineer-hours; no SLA credit.

B) Preserve in-place caching (higher cost): convert Dedicated instance to a smaller Dedicated reservation (if available in region) and apply a temporary seat credit for 1 month. This avoids KV loss but costs ~20% of the original committed monthly spend for the smaller footprint.

Ben and Lauren — can you draft a pricing appendix with numbers pulled from Alex's Q3 export? Alex — we'll propose the decision tree and the amendment language by Thursday EOD.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, Alex Torres <atorres@wellpath.health>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tier portability and fallback playbook — pricing scenarios

Alex / Irene — I ran a quick pass on Wellpath's Q3 export. Two pricing scenarios below with simple math for illustration (rounded).

Assumptions from file: avg 120k tokens/day, peak 350k tokens/day (12% of requests are low-latency routes using Dedicated GPUs).

Scenario 1 — Hosted fallback (A):
- Monthly hosted spend (current usage profile): ~$8,200
- Transition costs (one-time pre-warm + runbook): $1,200 (fixed)
- Expected perf delta for low-latency routes: +20–40 ms p50
- Proration/credits: pro-rata credit for any unused Dedicated commit; no stepdown fee if notice given 14 days in advance.

Scenario 2 — Small Dedicated reservation (B):
- Committed monthly seat (smaller): $6,400 (20% of original reserved)
- Temporary seat credit applied month 1: -$1,280 (20% credit)
- Migration labor: included in credit for month 1
- KV preserved; latency intact; no cold-start impact.

Next steps: 
- If you care most about absolute latency and zero cold starts, Recommendation = Scenario 2.
- If cost predictability + flexibility is priority, Recommendation = Scenario 1.

Irene — attaching a short checklist we can slip into the amendment. I also added the formula we use for pro-rata credits.

Attachments: redwood-amendment-draft.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

— Ben

Thanks — that framing is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from Procurement: 

- The procurement team needs an explicit definition of "top-3 routes" (we run about 18 distinct endpoints). Can you confirm if that's by token volume or by qps?
- If we choose Scenario 2, will the temporary seat credit require a separate amendment signature or can it be an SOW line item? Procurement prefers fewer docs.

Sally Greene (cc) will own the contract language. We can run a short 30-minute technical workshop if the team needs to validate the pre-warm plan.

I'll upload a short mapping of our endpoints later today.

Best,
Alex

- Contract mechanics: temporary seat credit can be included as a line item in the existing SOW (no separate amendment required) — we'll add the line and the proration formula.
